A1.justification: Despite v3's new title, both PDFs describe the same authors' PACT reconstruction framework and retain matching experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v3 includes supplementary Sections S1–S4; v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical simulations and reconstruction results using leaf-phantom and in vivo mouse-liver measurements, including Figs. 3–5.

after.justification: v3 reports original neural-field and pixel-grid reconstructions, five-phantom benchmarks and ablation results in Table 1, Figs. 4–6 and Figs. S2–S4.

M1.justification: v3 adds direct pixel-grid SOS optimization alongside the neural field. It replaces v1's reported 64-neuron, 4,417-parameter network with a 256-feature, 1,027-parameter configuration and removes explicit TV regularization from the neural-field objective while retaining it for the pixel grid. The differentiable physical model and multichannel inversion remain.

E1.justification: The simulation inputs are revised: v3 uses a more elaborate vascular initial-pressure image and evaluates different arrangements of high- and low-SOS regions representing bone, liver and stomach lumen (Fig. S4). This modestly broadens acoustic configurations within the retained 2D task. The measured leaf-phantom and mouse-liver datasets remain.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain conventional DAS, Dual-SOS DAS, APACT and the SOS oracle, while adding the proposed pixel-grid alternative alongside the neural field (Figs. 4–5 and Table 1). The delay comparison also expands from v1's neural-field-only study to neural field, pixel grid, APACT and oracle in v3 Fig. 6.

E3.justification: The default delay count changes from 32 to 16 and the neural-field learning rate from 0.001 to 0.1. v3 specifies a separate 30-epoch pixel-grid protocol, aggregates evaluation over five phantoms and adds SOS SSIM reporting. The mouse-liver DAS assumption changes from 1515 to 1517 m/s. Fig. 3d now evaluates oracle-based deconvolution rather than v1's complete reconstruction.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative pixel-grid TV-weight and neural-network-capacity studies (Figs. S2–S3), replacing v1's brief assertion of similar performance across architectures with explicit sensitivity evidence. It also expands the existing delay study from 4–32 channels to a multi-method 2–64-channel comparison (Fig. 6), examining reconstruction quality and computational tradeoffs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3's averages across five distinct phantoms are benchmark aggregation, without uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Fig. 4 reports neural-field IP PSNR/SSIM of 25.18/0.557 in 1.1 minutes; v3 Fig. 4 reports 25.04/0.504 in 40.0 seconds. These are replaced measurements under revised phantom and method settings, not comparable performance gains or losses. v3 adds pixel-grid, multi-phantom and ablation results. Some new entries conflict: pixel-grid sample-1 IP PSNR is 25.05 in Fig. 4 but 24.35 in Fig. S4.

T1.justification: The straight-ray assumption, wavefront-to-PSF equations and pseudoinverse formulation are retained. Supplement S2 explicitly writes out the Fourier expansion already discussed in v1 and explains APACT's harmonic truncation, without introducing a substantive new derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v3 broadens the advertised framework from NF-APACT to joint reconstruction supporting either pixel-grid or neural-field SOS representations, explicitly emphasizing representation and regularizer flexibility. The central claims of self-supervised recovery, superior reconstruction quality and an order-of-magnitude speed advantage remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains pixel-grid stripe artifacts through the path-integral wavefront calculation and discusses how neural-network capacity controls implicit smoothing and reconstruction failures. This qualifies v1's broad architecture-insensitivity statement. The original interpretations of image shrinkage, anatomical alignment and potential extension beyond the demonstrated 2D setting are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies the RTX A6000 GPU, specifies uniform delay sampling over [-0.8, 0.8] mm and provides fuller Gaussian-window stitching and normalization instructions. It documents pixel-grid hyperparameters and routes code access through a project page. Much of S1's acquisition and calibration information was already present in v1; the expanded stitching description does not establish a changed procedure.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises neural-field positioning, replacing generic NeRF examples with discussion of recent sparse/limited-view PACT representations, ultrasound SOS estimation and neural adaptive optics. Section 2 explicitly distinguishes prior constant-SOS, IP-only reconstruction from this work's joint recovery and relates its computational correction to existing neural wavefront methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution list are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes a separate section, neural-field parameterization is incorporated into joint reconstruction, and experimental details move into supplementary sections. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond simply adding experiments.

P2.justification: Fig. 1 is redesigned and gains a performance plot; Figs. 4–5 are restructured to include pixel-grid results and additional annotations. v3 adds Table 1, Fig. 6 and supplementary figures, including overlays that redisplay existing reconstructions. The journal-style headers, typography and page layout are also replaced.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the neural representation's role through the pixel-grid comparison and controlled regularization and capacity studies, addressing a central weakness of v1's largely asserted architectural benefits. Broader acoustic configurations and fuller implementation details improve validation and reproducibility. Inconsistent main-text/supplementary scores and the conflicting TV-weight statement in S3.2 weaken precise quantitative reproducibility, but the added controls and clearer account of failure conditions still provide a substantial net improvement.
